paper.title_en: Local response theory of multiparameter sudden-quench quantum Otto engines
paper.abstract_en: Multiparameter quantum Otto engines raise an optimization problem absent in single-parameter cycles: which small quench vector maximizes the quadratic approximation to the exact output work in a multidimensional control space? We develop a local response theory for sudden-quench Otto engines with quantum working media described by linearly controlled Hamiltonians. We show that the local quadratic work decomposes into a thermal-bias gain and a quadratic response cost, whose competition determines the quench vector that maximizes the local quadratic work at a prescribed quench amplitude. We illustrate the theory in a minimal two-level working medium, where radial and transverse quenches play distinct roles, and in a finite interacting XYZ spin chain, where the resulting quench vector is determined by the balance between thermal-bias and response cost. Our results provide a practical local criterion for designing small multiparameter quenches in sudden-quench quantum Otto engines.
